text:
mike: Heads-up: we're seeing ~38 GPUs in eu-west-2 stuck in provisioning after last night's BMC firmware push. Nodes boot but never signal ready, autoscaler queued.
anya: Ack. I saw the alerts — autoscaler hit cap and started queuing pods. Any BMC logs?
leo: Quick dump from one affected node (rack-23-11):
```
[2024-11-12T03:14:22Z] bmc: wake_request queued (id=0x4a)
[2024-11-12T03:14:22Z] bmc: sleep_state -> waking
[2024-11-12T03:14:23Z] bmc: wake_complete delayed: queue_len=12
[2024-11-12T03:14:40Z] bmc: secureboot_flag read=1 expected=1
[2024-11-12T03:14:40Z] bmc: kernel handoff timeout
```
sam: Interesting — queue_len=12 seems high. Other nodes show queue_len=0-2 during earlier rollouts.
mike: I also grabbed ipmi from a node that stayed down: `ipmitool -H 10.42.5.12 -U admin -P **** chassis power status` returns `Chassis Power is on` but provisioning agent times out on ssh.
anya: Could be BMC processing latency + network backplane congestion. Any secureboot toggles observed?
leo: One node shows `secureboot_flag read=1 expected=0` in a different log; looks like inconsistent state across fleet. Not a full toggle but read drift.
sam: Possible race: BMC wakes but doesn't release OOB DB entry causing subsequent wake requests to queue. That delays provisioning agents beyond timeouts.
infra-bot: deploybot: Firmware rollout to eu-west-2 completed 2024-11-12T02:50Z for image v1.4.3 (batch=all). Rollout ID: fw-roll-20241112-23
mike: Rollout was batch=all — that's why impact was broad. We should never do all-region pushes without canary on oob layer.
anya: Immediate mitigation: 1) pause any remaining firmware batches (done) 2) run targeted wake/thaw on queued nodes 3) revert to v1.4.2 if a quick hotfix not available.
sam: I ran `oobctl wake --force rack-23-11` on a few nodes, they cycled and came up. But 5 nodes still hung and required manual BMC power cycle.
leo: Manual steps I used: `ipmitool chassis power cycle` then `sleep 15` then `oobctl check-health`. That brought 3 of 5 back.
mike: Cost/impact note: provision backlog kept Dedicated pools partially idle for ~45m; estimate additional cloud spend ~ $1200 for fallback capacity.
anya: Root cause hypothesis: v1.4.3 introduced a change to the wake-queue handling that only surfaces under high parallel wake rates (our batch=all). It also has a subtle secureboot-state read/write race.
sam: Agreed. Action items: - Firmware team to triage wake-queue logic and secureboot read/writes (cc @firmware-team) - Create rollback runbook for BMC at scale - Add pre-roll canary that sends concurrent wake bursts to a small rack to validate queue behavior
leo: I'll open an incident ticket and add logs + node list. Ticket: INC-20241112-73
mike: For short-term: schedule a controlled rollback to v1.4.2 in eu-west-2 at 02:00 UTC tomorrow, with canary rack-01 first. Also set autoscaler max to current capacity to avoid double-provisioning while we stabilize.
anya: I'll notify customers on Dedicated affected by this window and update status page. :warning:
infra-bot: oncall: Reminder to file postmortem once incident is resolved.
sam: One more note — let's add BMC queue_len metric and alarm when >5 for >2m. That would've caught this earlier.
leo: I'll add the metric and a Grafana panel. Also adding an oob preflight check to rollout pipeline: small burst wake test + secureboot-read consistency check.
mike: Good. We'll follow up in the incident ticket. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
